titleEn: Sheep into the Pen, Time to Sleep!

pages.text: "Not bedtime yet! More rolling!" Pipo rolled the wooden ball in the yard. Sheep filed into the pen. "Once more, just once more!" he called with his mouth wide, almost yawning.
Closing the gate, Mom said, "Pipo, sheep in the pen means bedtime." "Not sleepy at all!" He shook his head and hugged the ball.
But his eyelids kept sinking. The ball kept slipping from his hands and rolling away. Yaaawn. "Oh? Am I a little sleepy...?" His eyes felt tired.
Mom held his hand and led him to the pen gate. Inside, sheep leaned together with eyes shut. She whispered, "Look, sheep into the pen, time to sleep!"
Getting ready began. First, brush by the well! Pipo rinsed with tub water and spat. Mom sang beside him, "Sheep into the pen, time to sleep!"
Second, under the covers! Pipo slipped into his little-room bed. The pen showed through the round window. Mom kissed his forehead and sang softly, "Sheep into the pen, time to sleep!"
Third, Mom blew out the yard lamp. Outside the round window, the pen was dark too, sheep breathing softly inside. Pipo's eyes slowly closed.
Pipo curled under the covers, both hands at his chest. Like the sheep outside, his eyes gently shut. The wooden ball beside his bed slept too.
Under the covers, he counted quietly. "One, sheep in the pen means stop playing! Two, brush, brush! Three, sleep under the covers!" Only his soft breathing sounded in the room.
Morning. Sheep said baa before the gate. Mom hugged Pipo. "A good sleep woke you with the sheep!" Sound sleep made morning light and easy. He called, "Sheep into the pen, time to sleep!"
